'''John 'Jack' Connor''' is a British theoretical physicist whose research focussed on understanding the physics of [[nuclear fusion]]. 

== Education ==
After studying for an undergraduate degree in Mathematical Physics at the University of Birmingham he gained a PhD in Elementary Particle Physics at the same university.<ref name=tokamakenergy>{{cite web |title=Our Team |url=https://www.tokamakenergy.co.uk/company/our-team/ |publisher=Tokamak Energy |access-date=1 October 2021}}</ref> 

== Career ==
In 1967 he began working at the [[Culham Centre for Fusion Energy]] in Oxfordshire where he remained until he retired in 2007.<ref name=tokamakenergy/> In 2004 he was awarded the [[Hannes Alfvén Prize]] alongside [[Jim Hastie (physicist)|Jim Hastie]] and [[John Bryan Taylor|Bryan Taylor]] due to their wide contributions to the development of theories critical to [[magnetic confinement fusion]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Lister |first1=Jo |title=Award of the 2004 Hannes Alfvén Prize of the European Physical Society to J W Connor, R J Hastie and J B Taylor |journal=Plasma Physics and Controlled Fusion |date=December 2004 |volume=46 |issue=12B |doi=10.1088/0741-3335/46/12B/E02 |bibcode=2004PPCF...46.....L |s2cid=250876267 |access-date=1 October 2021|url=https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2004PPCF...46.....L/abstract}}</ref> 

== Recognition ==
In 2010 he was elected a Fellow of the Royal Society for his contributions to the field, in particular for his work in the 1970s demonstrating that a plasma confined in a [[tokamak]] can produce its own current, termed the [[bootstrap current]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Jack Connor |url=https://royalsociety.org/people/jack-connor-11259/ |publisher=The Royal Society |access-date=1 October 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Sloan |first1=Liam |title=Scientist elected to leading society |url=https://www.oxfordmail.co.uk/news/8206195.scientist-elected-leading-society/ |access-date=1 October 2021 |work=Oxford Mail |date=7 June 2010}}</ref> This discovery is the basis of all modern tokamak reactors, including [[ITER]].<ref>{{cite web |title=2008 Payne-Gaposchkin medal and prize |url=https://www.iop.org/about/awards/subject/payne_gaposchkin-/medallists/page_38581.html |publisher=Institute of Physics |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150906093914/https://www.iop.org/about/awards/subject/payne_gaposchkin-/medallists/page_38581.html |access-date=1 October 2021|archive-date=2015-09-06 }}</ref>
